## Company: Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI)
Sector: Financials / Banks
Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) was incorporated on January 4, 1943, as a domestic commercial bank and went public on October 12, 1971. The Company offers an array of financial services that include corporate banking, consumer banking, investment banking, asset management, corporate finance, securities distribution, and insurance services.

The Company's principal subsidiaries are BPI Capital Corp.; BPI Direct BanKo, Inc.; BPI Asset Management and Trust Corporation; BPI Wealth Hongkong Limited; BPI (Europe) Plc (BPI Europe); BPI Investments Inc.; BPI Remittance Centre Hong Kong Ltd. (BERC HK); BPI Wealth Singapore Pte. Ltd.; Legazpi Savings Bank, Inc.; and BPI/MS Insurance Corp.

As of December 31, 2024, BPI operates 1,266 branches nationwide and 1,876 automated teller machines and cash accept machines. Overseas, the Company has two banking subsidiaries, BERC HK in Hong Kong and BPI Europe in London.

Source: SEC Form 17-A (2024)

thesis:
BPI is a well-understood business. It takes deposits, makes loans, manages wealth, and earns on the spread — a model unchanged in its essentials across economic cycles. The Philippines remains structurally underbanked relative to regional peers, giving BPI a long runway in a market it already dominates. Q1 2026 revenues hit ₱50.9 billion (+13.9% YoY), net income ₱16.9 billion (+1.7% YoY), with net interest margins expanding 7 basis points to 4.57%. The business is squarely within any generalist investor's circle of competence. Founded in 1851 as Banco Español-Filipino, BPI is the oldest bank in Southeast Asia.

The moat is real and multi-layered. BPI's 1,266-branch network and brand — reinforced by its recent dual ISO certification and inclusion in Forbes' 2026 World's Top Performing Banks — creates deep switching-cost advantages. Filipinos rarely change banks. The moat also extends into the digital era: BPI's move to make interbank transfers permanently free from July 1 is aggressive customer acquisition that smaller rivals cannot easily absorb. The stablecoin remittance pilot with Meridian (targeting the $40B OFW corridor) signals management thinking ahead on a structural opportunity, not reacting. These are moat-widening moves, not desperation plays.

Management under CEO Limcaoco earns a qualified pass. Moody's affirmed BPI's deposit ratings in May 2026 on "strong profitability and asset quality" — a third-party credibility anchor. But Q1 missed EPS forecasts (₱3.2 vs. ₱3.47), and management revised credit cost guidance upward to 90–100 bps, citing Middle East tensions and retail borrower stress. The NPL ratio climbed to 2.42% (problem loan ratio 3.4% end-2025), with SME NPLs particularly elevated at 12.5% — construction and non-essential goods sectors showing stress. These aren't fabricated surprises; management disclosed them promptly and revised guidance accordingly. No red flags on honesty, but execution risk on asset quality is elevated.

Valuation is where a strict Rule #1 discipline forces a hard stop. The Sticker Price of ₱94.56 sits below today's ₱103.10 — meaning you're already paying above Phil Town's fair value. The MOS buy price of ₱47.28 is more than 50% below current price, a gap that requires either a dramatic market dislocation or a sustained earnings collapse to close. That said, P/E of 8.2x, P/B of 1.1x, and a PEG of 0.69x are objectively cheap on bank valuation norms. The 4.2% dividend provides meaningful return while you wait. The tension is real: the stock looks cheap by traditional bank metrics but fails the margin of safety test that Rule #1 demands. Rising credit costs and slowing net income growth (1.7% in Q1 vs. 13.8% 10-year average) suggest the near-term earnings engine is sputtering — precisely when you'd want a larger discount, not a premium.

BPI is an exceptional franchise with a durable moat, credible management, and a long-term growth story tied to Philippine financial deepening and OFW remittance flows. But at ₱103.10 — above fair value with asset quality under visible pressure — the risk-reward is unfavorable for a new position. Watch for the price to pull back toward the ₱85–90 range (closer to sticker price) or for NPL trends to clearly stabilize and credit costs to normalize below 80 bps. Either development would shift this to a buy.

verification.notes: BPI was founded Aug 1, 1851 as Banco Español-Filipino de Isabel II; the current entity was incorporated in 1943. Both are true, so this is correctly a non-error.
